used_notes: Yes - the raw notes changed several judgements that the statistics alone would have gotten wrong: they showed that many high-count candidates (C-48 kestrel-v2 19 false-alarm reports, C-45 veridian-hub 13 reports) are actually one loud site (every entity-bearing note comes from R01S00), that C-17 nimbus-lite's 17 data-exposure reports are a single-day fan-out on d082 sitting on top of one site's routine policy traffic, that C-29 osprey-pay470's and C-28 tundrax's impressive source counts are same-day, word-for-word broadcast copies, and - most decisively - that roughly a third of candidates (C-1, C-3, C-13, C-18, C-19, C-21, C-22, C-31, C-32, C-33, C-35, C-36, C-46, C-51) have link statistics that no note actually attributes to the named entity at all, while conversely confirming that C-9, C-39 and C-58 really do have each link reported by a different region.
reasoning_notes:
Method: for each candidate I (a) mapped its links onto the seven causal chains and checked whether they sit on ONE chain and whether first_seen_day respects that chain's order; (b) read every source note and counted only those that name the candidate entity AND carry a synonym for one of its events - notes about other entities are background traffic and were discounted even when the aggregate counts looked strong; (c) checked the REGION-SITE-DEPT-TEAM-USER prefixes of the attesting notes to see whether a link's reporters really span the organisation or collapse onto one site, one team, or one user; (d) penalised identical note text repeated across org paths on a single day (broadcast echo rather than independent discovery).

Top tier: C-9 arbor-na carries all six links of the supply chain (supplier_substitution d6 -> component_defect d20 -> yield_drop d30 -> shipment_delay d57 -> customer_escalation d50-134 -> revenue_miss d93), each link attested by entity-named notes from a different region (R04, R02, R06, R04). C-39 nimbusx532 is the cleanest auth chain: cert_rotation d52 (R01) -> auth_failure d60 (R00) -> api_error_spike d70 (R04) -> checkout_drop d97 (R06) -> revenue_miss d120 (R01), one link per region, in order. C-0 peregrine and C-20 sable are compliance chains with entity-named notes from six and seven regions respectively. C-12 basalt and C-58 zephyr-core495 walk the attrition chain end to end with a different region behind each step. C-6 solace-pay and C-7 kestrel-pay are ordered supply chains with wide spread. C-53 tundra (network -> latency -> batch overrun), C-38 zephyr-pay, C-41 umbra-pay, C-2 pellucid and C-40 lumen-pay are somewhat thinner but still single-chain, in order and genuinely cross-organisational.

Rejected despite good-looking statistics: C-48 kestrel-v2 and C-45 veridian-hub (all entity notes from region R01 site S00 - one loud site's routine traffic); C-17 nimbus-lite (nine sources, but the entire data_exposure_risk link fires on day 082 and the policy_change link is one site, R00S02); C-29 osprey-pay470 (eleven policy reports and eleven workaround reports that are literally the same sentence repeated on d072 and d078); C-28 tundrax (supplier_substitution and yield_drop are each a single-day burst confined to region R06, and the revenue_miss link has no attesting note); C-56 quarry-pay (well attested but account_churn d10 precedes sla_breach d11 and backlog_growth d14 - the chain runs backwards); C-10 cobalt-core and C-8 meridianx (coherent-looking chains whose notes name a different entity - cobalt-pay, meridian-edge); C-44 umbra and C-25 basalt-core (two links, out of causal order).

Bottom: candidates whose links are scattered over unrelated chains and/or have no note naming the entity at all - C-46 solacex is the extreme case, seven links spanning five different chains with not one corroborating note.
